decision: Use a worker-side signed request adapter over the bounded stdio transport, with persistent reserve-before-sign counters and one framed request/response exchange per invocation

evaluatedApproaches.name: persistent-signer-plus-framed-stdio-client
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: preserves worker HMAC identity, durable monotonic anti-replay counters, fenced lease tokens, and deterministic request/response framing
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: fails closed on malformed/truncated responses and composes with coordinator replay fencing after worker restart
evaluatedApproaches.latency: one signing operation, one small counter persistence, and one framed exchange per request
evaluatedApproaches.resourceUse: low constant memory and constant-size local counter state
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: low-medium because it wraps existing signer and transport contracts without changing queue semantics
evaluatedApproaches.qa: end-to-end tests cover claim/complete, worker restart, duplicate replay rejection, and truncated transport behavior

evaluatedApproaches.name: raw-worker-calls-with-manual-counters
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: callers can accidentally reuse or regress counters and bypass the intended client contract
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: weak under restart and concurrent worker processes
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: high correctness risk due to duplicated protocol logic

evaluatedApproaches.name: long-lived-multiplexed-session
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: can be correct with correlation IDs and ordered response handling
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: requires session recovery, correlation state, half-open handling, and more complex partition semantics
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: medium-high before qrexec deployment behavior is measured
evaluatedApproaches.qa: deferred until real-worker throughput requires multiplexing

evaluatedApproaches.name: network-http-client
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: mature request semantics but introduces a network service boundary not required by the current Qubes model
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: adds TLS, listener, firewall, and certificate lifecycle requirements
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: high for the current isolation-first architecture

whyItWon: It closes the missing worker-side integration path using the already-selected authentication, replay, lease-fencing, and stdio framing primitives. It has the smallest new attack surface and regression surface while remaining directly adaptable to a Qubes qrexec launcher.
knownFailuresAndLessons: A transport failure after the coordinator accepted a mutation can leave the worker uncertain whether the action committed; mission mutations therefore still need safe retry semantics and idempotency where applicable.

A truncated response test intentionally demonstrates this ambiguity: the claim may be committed even though the worker did not receive the response. Lease expiry/recovery limits damage, but an explicit request-id/result lookup protocol would improve recovery.
The client does not itself launch qrexec; deployment-specific process invocation and policy remain outside this module.
Persistent counters prevent replay but state rollback/loss still requires controlled worker re-enrollment.

REAL-WORKER readiness still requires actual qrexec service/policy installation, secret provisioning/rotation, multi-Qube crash/partition tests, and an ambiguity-recovery protocol for committed requests with lost responses.
